title: Including the first argument of checkNotNull in the failure message is not useful, as it will always be `null`.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Preconditions only accepts the %s placeholder in error message strings.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Prefer calling overloads that accept a Charset over those that accept a String encoding name.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Prefer instanceof over getKind() checks where possible, as these work well with pattern matching instanceofs.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Prefer using java.time-based APIs when available. Note that this checker does not and cannot guarantee that the overloads have equivalent semantics, but that is generally the case with overloaded methods.
summary: It is an experimental check, so Error Prone does not turn it on by default.

title: Consider using Preconditions instead of explicit if-throw for parameter validation.
summary: It is an experimental check, so Error Prone does not turn it on by default.

title: Prefer the @throws javadoc tag instead of @exception.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: This type can be more specific.
summary: It is an experimental check, so Error Prone does not turn it on by default.

title: Passing a primitive array to a varargs method is usually wrong.
summary: It is an experimental check, so Error Prone does not turn it on by default.

title: Using compareAndSet with boxed primitives is dangerous, as reference rather than value equality is used. Consider using AtomicInteger, AtomicLong, AtomicBoolean from JDK or AtomicDouble from Guava instead.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Add a private constructor to modules that will not be instantiated by Dagger.
summary: It is an experimental check, so Error Prone does not turn it on by default.

title: Classes which are not intended to be instantiated should be made non-instantiable with a private constructor. This includes utility classes (classes with only static members), and the main class.
summary: It is an experimental check, so Error Prone does not turn it on by default.

title: Access to a private protocol buffer field is forbidden. This protocol buffer carries a security contract, and can only be created using an approved library. Direct access to the fields is forbidden.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Protected members in final classes can be package-private.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Unnecessary call to proto's #build() method. If you don't consume the return value of #build(), the result is discarded and the only effect is to verify that all required fields are set, which can be expressed more directly with #isInitialized().
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: GetNanos() only accesses the underlying nanosecond-adjustment of the duration.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Comparing protobuf fields of type String using reference equality.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: GetNanos() only accesses the underlying nanosecond-adjustment of the instant.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: The arguments passed to `ignoringFields` are inconsistent with the proto which is the subject of the assertion.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: To get the tag number of a protocol buffer enum, use getNumber() instead.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: @Provides methods need to be declared in a Module to have any effect.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.
